iconicAnchor.label: Early printed-book woodcuts
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: European relief-print and book illustration traditions
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The Library of Congress demonstrates how raised carved lines print black, cut areas remain white, the image reverses, and woodblocks integrate naturally with relief-set type.

sources.title: Woodcut
supports: Woodcut is a relief process in which raised carved surfaces receive ink while recessed cuts remain unprinted.

sources.title: Heavenly Craft: The Woodcut in Early Printed Books
supports: Woodcut line, negative cutting, reversal, press transfer, and integration with movable type shaped early narrative book imagery.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches carved relief line, heavy black shape, white cut mark, compressed figure ground, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/narrative-woodcut/reference-01.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
